videos.title: Water Polo Strength & Conditioning
videos.overview: Comprehensive dryland and in-water conditioning series covering active dynamic mobility, resistance-band rotator cuff prehab, core rotation, and in-water wrestling, positioning, and partner endurance drills.

videos.title: Water Polo 2m Position
videos.overview: Center forward (hole set) and 2-meter defender battles: ball-side positioning, hand-fighting, split eggbeater leverage, turning/sealing, drawing exclusions, defensive recovery.

videos.title: Water Polo Offense
videos.overview: Perimeter driving, releases, and defender manipulation: separation against a press, feeding the center, fast-twitch direction changes.

videos.title: Water Polo Defense
videos.overview: Perimeter press defense, tactical fouling, drop/crash positioning, driver denial. High hips, forearm leverage, perimeter awareness.

videos.title: Water Polo Passing and Shooting
videos.overview: Live passing, ball protection under pressure, beating splitters, shoulder fakes and hitches, finishing releases.

videos.title: Water Polo Fundamentals
videos.overview: Aquatic movement, eggbeater mechanics, elevation, horizontal-to-vertical balance, slide-and-shoot progressions.

videos.title: USAWP Base Position Fundamentals
videos.overview: The base position for faking, passing and shooting: tripod legs and left arm, chest forward, shoulders 30-45° off the goal, elbow at ear height behind the shoulder line, wrist facing the target; the mistakes that break it; internal rotation; and the drills that build it.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Eggbeater
videos.overview: The eggbeater as ODP teaches it: balanced start, wide base, high knees, flat feet.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Repeat Breaststroke Kicks
videos.overview: Short fast breaststroke kicks from a 45° chest angle as the only power source, then the reach lunge.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Spidering technique
videos.overview: Working efficiently in the horizontal position, hips above chest, ready to explode.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Skating + Lunging
videos.overview: Explosive 45° glides from the horizontal position, then the reach lunge that helps back to the center.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Reverse Sculling
videos.overview: Moving backward on the hip with the legs doing the work: the base of the zone position, drive defense and inside water.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP ball handling drills
videos.overview: Warm-up, station or variety work with the ball: balance, core, legs and hand-eye.

clips.title: Series Introduction & Training Philosophy
cues: Overview of the multi-module system: dryland mobility, functional strength, in-water body movement, perimeter play, center play, fitness.

clips.title: Active Dynamic Stretching Protocol
cues: Dynamic, continuous movement over static holding.
Full-body: shoulders, thoracic spine, groin, hip flexors, knees, wrists, ankles.

clips.title: Upper-Body Mobility: Arm Swings, Butterfly & Elbow Spins
cues: Forward/reverse arm circles (6–12 each); two-arm butterfly swings; elbow spins and wrist rotations (shot snap); single-arm rotational swings into throwing posture.

clips.title: Lower-Body Mobility: Hips, Groin & Hamstring Series
cues: Seated quad/hip pulls; butterfly stretch, partner-assisted hamstring; supine spinal twist; high-knee chest pulls replicating eggbeater chambering.

clips.title: Resistance Band Shoulder Prehab Routine
cues: 15 min before every water workout.
Scarecrow row; elbow-pinned internal/external rotations at steady cadence; standing fake-throw with core rotation; triceps snap-through.

clips.title: In-Water Resistance: Arm Lock Drill
cues: Body contact while protecting the ball; torso at 45°; split eggbeater — lead leg straight down under shoulders, back leg at 45° driving forward.

clips.title: Conditioning & Wrestling: Dead Man Swimming Drill
cues: Groups of three; two wrestle 5–10 s, sprint to wall on whistle; winner rests, loser stays in against the fresh player.
Cut off pursuit angles, keep the opponent on your back/hip.

clips.title: Tactical Water Protection: The Human Shield Drill
cues: Protect an open ball without touching it; back to defender; continuous split eggbeater; elbows out in a straight line = "your water"; never swing elbows back past the midline.

clips.title: Center Trench Warfare Philosophy
cues: Games are won at center.
Winning ball side forces the defense into a drop, opening driving and outside shooting lanes.

clips.title: Ball Control Drill (BC Drill)
cues: Ball stays within the shoulder frame; hands slide under, never slap over; split eggbeater — one leg vertical, opposite leg at 45° behind.
Ball outside the frame = a steal.

clips.title: Defend Your Opponent Drill (DYO Drill)
cues: Control the jumping defender before going to the ball.
Breaststroke kick to seal the attacked side; near shoulder wedges, far hand controls the ball; head up for crashers and goalie.

clips.title: Face Turn & Seal Drill
cues: Ball on the weak-side triangle (1–2), center faces the strong side (4–5).
The moment the ball enters the strong side: under-armpit hook, rotate hips, seal before the pass arrives — or it is an offensive foul.

clips.title: Stroke & Spin vs. Stroke & Slip
cues: Fronted tight: fake a hard stroke, chin to chest, whitewater, spin 180° behind the defender.
Separation: skip the spin, slip the inside arm under the armpit and kick through. (Slip at `00:06:33`.)

clips.title: 2m Defender: Suit Grab Spin-Out & Forearm Control
cues: Release body contact first, then spin laterally to ball side.
Forearm contact on the set's back/shoulder, not wrist or waist — take the game out of the referee's hands.

clips.title: 2m Defender: Absorb & Lunge Drill
cues: Don't drop vertical when the set backs down.
Stay at 45°, absorb with high hips; when the set squares to shoot, explode off a breaststroke kick to contest.

clips.title: 2m Defender: Jump Inside Control Drill
cues: Beaten inside: never swim over the back (exclusion or 5 m).
Stay horizontal, breaststroke kick around the side, inside hand hooks the armpit, outside hand up clean to deflect.

clips.title: Perimeter Philosophy & Fast-Twitch Manipulation
cues: Make the defender commit weight and hips one way, exploit the counter-momentum.
Fast-twitch over slow swimming.

clips.title: Fast-Twitch Drive & Step-Back Release
cues: Sell 2–3 explosive strokes; as the defender commits and drops hips, step back over your hips into the vertical. 1–2 m of separation to feed set or shoot.

clips.title: Advanced Release (Ball-Side Hip Rotation)
cues: Two strokes to the ball carrier; rotate hips flat along the surface (don't drop them); shins and knees brace into the defender underwater; control the ball with the outside hand.

clips.title: Dig & Pop Drill
cues: High-cadence slip strokes sell the drive; defender drops vertical; jump back over your legs into a high eggbeater to catch and redirect or feed.

clips.title: Two-Stroke Release for Smaller Players
cues: Sweep the inside arm across the defender's chest; the forearm becomes a shield; split eggbeater absorbs contact and keeps the passing window open.

clips.title: Right-Back Drill
cues: One crossing stroke to show the referee the hold, pop the chest out and return the ball live without stalling the clock.

clips.title: Drive-Up Release & High Post
cues: Teammate drives down, you drive up into the vacant lane to balance the water; horizontal swim → protective vertical wall.
High-post: receive at 5 m, draw the foul, direct shot.

clips.title: Stunt Move
cues: Shake-and-bake: fast-twitch head/torso fake with whitewater, cut back against the defender's momentum, trail hand clears the hip.
Also keeps your defender from helping.

clips.title: Elbow Control & Inside Stroke Mechanics
cues: Outside hand locks the defender's elbow/triceps, inside hand takes a full stroke.
Own the elbow, own the torso angle.
If he spins, step back over hips or cut across his back inside.

clips.title: Grind & Shin Release
cues: Inside stroke plus hip contact, then shins slide up the defender's torso and push off cleanly.
Never kick with the bottom of the foot (contra-foul).

clips.title: Perimeter Defensive Principles
cues: Two breakdowns: losing ball-vs-man awareness, and dropping hips vertical (drivers spin or push off).

clips.title: Standard Absorbed Shoulder Control
cues: Lead hand/forearm on the attacker's lead shoulder while he holds the ball; body at 45° via breaststroke kick; the instant he releases, both hands up clean.

clips.title: The Slip Move Steal
cues: Attacker relaxes: breaststroke kick inside, knock the ball off the hand/elbow with the lead arm, raise the controlling arm to show no foul.

clips.title: Foul & Deny Drill
cues: Lunge, hit the elbow, tactical foul; rotate hips straight back into a 45° denial (split eggbeater); near hand takes the lane to set, trail arm sculls for height against the lob.

clips.title: Foul-to-Foul Drill
cues: Against the right-back: don't sit in denial; rotate over hips, second breaststroke kick, knock him down and foul again before a live entry.

clips.title: Foul & Crash Drill
cues: Their set has position: foul your man, spin over your hips, swim straight into the 2 m crash lane to double.

clips.title: Extra Stroke Drill (Driver Defense at 2 Meters)
cues: Driver stops at the 2 m line: don't rest on his outside shoulder and reach over (5 m or exclusion).
The line is another defender — two extra strokes around, hips along the surface, take inside water.

clips.title: Inside 4-Meter Pressing Drill
cues: Unbroken contact with forearms, elbows or chest; head swivels man–ball; contact lost → find the man first, then the ball.
Hips up, never vertical.

clips.title: Passing Mastery & Setting the Defense
cues: Great passers freeze defenders until the last moment.
Horizontal → 45° keeps passing angles live; if the defender doesn't value you, you are wasting the open man.

clips.title: Step-Away Passing (Weak Side)
cues: Defender lunges to your strong side: step away.
Ball over the head, or a 360° eggbeater spin releasing without hesitation.

clips.title: Step to Strong Side (Cross-Face Reception)
cues: Cross-face catch exposes the blind side.
Step across into a split eggbeater diving to the strong side; off-hand digs laterally; breaststroke kick up and over the defender's hands.

clips.title: Step to Weak Side vs. Blindsiding Splitter
cues: Vertical → horizontal dive to the weak side; breaststroke kick clears the trailing arm; off-hand shields for half a second.

clips.title: Step-Back Pass to Set
cues: Against a zone knock-down: drop onto your back only momentarily (the 2 m defender can step out and steal), then snap hips and legs under and launch vertical to pass or shoot.

clips.title: Step-In Pass & Shoulder Hitching
cues: Attack the cage with the arm high so the splitter must commit; hitch the shoulders to make the goalie jump; slip the wrist pass to the open shooter.

clips.title: Shooting Mechanics: Fast-Twitch Shoulder Fakes
cues: Twitch the lead shoulder and release immediately.
Ball stays behind or above the head; bringing it forward costs the re-cock and lets goalie and blocker reset.

clips.title: Cross-Face Near-Side Shot
cues: Shoulders pre-aligned to the cage, not the passer; catch and release with zero hesitation before the goalie slides.

clips.title: Cross-Face Draw Shot
cues: Body horizontal, legs moving with the ball; step across to open a new lane, draw goalie and blocker near-side, snap the wrist cross-cage.

clips.title: Shooting Summary: Release Angles & Variety
cues: Quickness and deceptive release beat velocity.
Wrap, overhead, wrist cross-cage, fast-twitch near side.

clips.title: Foundations of In-Water Agility
cues: Seamless horizontal ↔ vertical transition is the foundation of every advanced skill.

clips.title: Treading Water & Eggbeater Mechanics
cues: Knees wide, thighs perpendicular to the surface at 90°; feet in independent circles, snapping; upper body still.
Error: piston/scissor kick → bobbing, no visual stability.

clips.title: Tabletop / Spider Drill
cues: Back flat on the surface; all four limbs sculling; legs = balance, arms = steering; quick 90° pivots.

clips.title: Slip Stroke Technique
cues: High-cadence freestyle recovery with high elbows, hands slice without pulling; legs coiled horizontal ready to kick away.

clips.title: Stepping Drill
cues: Body in a straight line at the surface; lead hand sculls, trail hand pulls to the hip.
Perimeter defenders sliding lanes; shooters stepping into pockets.

clips.title: Absorb & Drag Drill
cues: Defender stays horizontal while driven backward; forearm on chest/shoulder with open hands visible; hips at the surface ready to kick out when the attacker goes to pass or shoot.

clips.title: Left & Right Hip Swings (180° Switches)
cues: Lead foot breaks the surface as the legs tuck tight under the torso; instant 180° redirection without dropping vertical.

clips.title: Pass, Slide, Catch & Shoot (H2 Dive Progression)
cues: Horizontal dive for 1–2 m into the lane, snap the foundation leg under to pop vertical, catch at peak height, finish.
Foundation leg = height, back leg = power.

clips.title: H2 Dive Counter-Attack Finishing
cues: Strokes with the ball, snap the lead leg under, quick dive to freeze the trailer, read the goalie, finish.

clips.title: Weak-Side Slide, Catch & Shoot
cues: Dive into the weak-side window before the ball arrives, shooting hand up during the slide, one-touch finish.
Shooters create their own movement.

clips.title: Why Fundamentals Win: Schroeder & Brooks
cues: Balance is the most important thing in athletics.
At Partizan the best coach worked only with the 10-and-unders, on balance in the water.
The pros shoot hard because they shoot accurately, and they shoot accurately because the base is sound.
Without fundamentals the game peaks.

clips.title: Base Position: The Tripod
cues: Start here every time you have the ball, whether faking, passing or shooting.
Left arm out to the left, left leg straight down, right leg slightly out to the right: a tripod.
Chest angled down, leaning forward.
Shoulders rotated 30-45° off the goal, never parallel.
Throwing shoulder pinched, elbow at ear height, wrist bent back and facing the goal.

clips.title: Common Base-Position Mistakes
cues: Over-rotating with the left shoulder pointed at the goal: inconsistent release point, slower release, more time for the goalie.
Legs too far under the shooting arm: you move laterally and cannot use the body for power or vary the release.
Lying on your back: easier, but no core in the finish, so you overshoot.

clips.title: Legs: Lift and Rudder; Lean Forward
cues: Open the legs as wide as possible.
The left leg carries the up-and-down load; the right leg is the rudder for lateral movement.
Chest faces the bottom so leg acceleration transfers forward into the shot.
Leaning forward is off balance by design; the left hand sculls to keep you from falling.
Start parallel to the goal and rotate the shoulders 30-45°.

clips.title: Elbow Behind the Shoulder Line
cues: Elbow at ear height, shoulder pinched, elbow always behind the line between the two shoulders.
This needs shoulder flexibility; over-rotating the body to fake it is the common error.
The wrist faces the goal wherever the arm is, so the full wrist motion is available at the end.

clips.title: The Wrist: The Finish
cues: The wrist faces the target at all times, from 90° back to all the way forward, and pushes through with all five fingers at once.
It sets accuracy and consistency.

clips.title: Common Wrist Mistakes
cues: Turning the wrist over on its side instead of facing the goal adds rotation into the motion and breaks consistency.

clips.title: Throwing Form at Full Speed
cues: Check the start: wrist forward, elbow at the ear, left hand slightly in front, shoulder pinched, chest forward.
The base does not change until the throw starts.
Sequence: hard breaststroke kick, internal rotation of the shoulder, wrist snap and follow-through.

clips.title: Base-Position Drills: Walks and Markers
cues: Walk 25 m and back holding the ball in base position; the position must not change, and the temptation is to over-rotate because it moves faster.
Same walk, eggbeater up and accelerate with the legs at every marker; the upper body must not move, so the legs learn to work apart from the torso.
Eggbeater down the pool at about 80%, then one hard breaststroke kick to full release height.

clips.title: Internal Rotation: Steal Time from the Goalie
cues: Internal rotation of the shoulder accelerates the release and adds power.
Timing is the game: accelerating at one point in the motion beats the goalie's reaction.
Isolate it before you combine it.

clips.title: Internal Rotation Drill
cues: Parallel to your partner, elbow at shoulder height, ball back, wrist bent.
Follow the internal rotation forward slowly until the ball touches the water in front of you; three or four reps, then pass with the same motion and full wrist extension.
Check: at the end, the elbow is not in front of the shoulder line.

clips.title: Wrist Drills: Deck Release and Hand-to-Hand
cues: On deck, shoulders parallel to the wall, release the ball over and over; the wrist faces the wall, bends all the way back and forward, and the release point off the fingers is the same every time.
In the water, walk down the pool eggbeatering and pass hand to hand with the wrists only; speed is irrelevant, full range and wrists facing each other are the point.

clips.title: Closing: Repetition Until It Is Natural
cues: Watching it and trying it twice changes nothing.
Repeat until the motion is automatic.
Body position in the water is the one fundamental that separates the best from the mediocre.

clips.title: ODP Eggbeater: Sitting in the Chair
cues: The most fundamental movement and the base for everything else.
Start balanced: Jesse Smith looks like he is sitting in a chair.
Wide base, wide hips, hip flexibility, knees high, feet flat.
The common youth error is pointed toes, which make no force.
Eggbeater, short breaststroke kicks, and the transition between them are the foundation of all movement in the water.

clips.title: Short Fast Breaststroke Kicks at 45°
cues: Chest at 45°, facing forward, hands out of the water, short fast breaststroke kicks as the only power source.
Laps of 25 m or yd with a break between, repeated.
Foundation for movement in the water and for a strong eggbeater.

clips.title: Add the Reach Lunge; Vary the Angle
cues: Once the 45° kick is strong, add a reach lunge to simulate the steal, knocking a player down, and explosive defensive position.
Game use: pressing without fouling, pressure on the ball, defense with the legs.
As athletes develop, run the same kicks from horizontal and vertical positions.
Every youth practice, every week.

clips.title: Spidering: Horizontal, Hips Above Chest
cues: On the stomach, body compact, all four limbs fast: hands scull and pull, legs eggbeater.
Chest down and hips higher than the chest so the body can spring into an explosive movement at any time.
Uses: helping on a ball-side drive, helping at center, lunging into a lane for the steal, horizontal defense on the wings at the bottom line.

clips.title: Spider to Reach Lunge
cues: From the spider, a breaststroke kick into a lunge: pull with the hands, breaststroke kick with the legs, reach with the arm for the steal.
Three limbs together.
Repeat weekly.

clips.title: Skating: Explosive 45° Glides
cues: Horizontal, stomach to the bottom, hips above chest.
Reach out and glide at 45° angles, from the eggbeater into an explosive breaststroke kick, two kicks per side, and see how much ground you cover.
Kick, pull and reach at the same time.
Watch your hands as a goalkeeper watches the block.
Game use: recovering in the zone, helping on defense, helping back on the center.

clips.title: Skate + Reach Lunge
cues: After the 45° skate, the lead hand pulls water, the legs breaststroke-kick, and the opposite arm reach-lunges as far as possible: helping back to steal the ball from the center.
Dynamic horizontal defense.

clips.title: Reverse Sculling ("Bicycling")
cues: On the side or hip, not the chest, body in a straight line in the direction of travel, moving backward.
Legs high: lead leg at the surface, bottom leg no more than two feet down, pedaling at a high rate; the legs do the vast majority of the work.
Bottom arm pushes water, top arm pulls.
Learn it on both hips.
Basis for the zone defensive base position, drive defense and attacking inside water.

clips.title: Dry-Ball Freestyle and Backstroke
cues: Freestyle with the ball in front of the face on a steady short breaststroke kick.
Backstroke with the ball above the head; variant with the ball dry in front in a water polo backstroke motion.
Balance, core strength, leg strength, hand-eye coordination.

clips.title: Ball in Hand
cues: Advance with the ball gripped in the hand, as if a defender were beside you.
Not everyone can grip it; strive for it.
Short breaststroke kicks throughout.
Stop into a vertical position as in transition or counterattack, then back to ball in hand.

clips.title: Elbow Swim
cues: Advance with the hand under the ball, not on top of it, on a short breaststroke kick.

clips.title: Hand Transfer in Transition
cues: Three or four head-up strokes with the ball, transfer from the weak hand to the strong hand above water, and immediately go vertical into a double-threat position: the counterattack with a defender closing.

clips.title: Pressure Passing
cues: Ball behind the head, breaststroke away from the defender to protect it, then up vertical to pass or shoot away from him.
Ball above the head at all times, short breaststroke kicks, never bring it in front of the face.

groups.title: Fundamentals — legs and body position
groups.description: Everything else sits on this. If your eggbeater bobs or your hips drop, no drive, release or shot works. Watch the bad eggbeater in the first clip once, then don't be that guy.

groups.title: Perimeter offense — releases and drives
groups.description: How we get open on the perimeter. Fast-twitch sells the drive; the step-back over your hips is what actually creates the pass. Start with the drive/step-back and dig-and-pop; the hip-rotation release and grind/shin are varsity.

groups.title: Perimeter defense — press, foul, deny
groups.description: Two ways we break down: losing ball-and-man, and dropping our hips. Hand on the shoulder while he has the ball, hands up the instant he passes. Foul-and-deny is our default when set has position.

groups.title: 2 m offense — ball control and sealing
groups.description: Ball stays inside the shoulders, hands under it. Control the defender before the ball. Face-turn and seal the moment the ball crosses into the strong side.

groups.title: 2 m defense — absorb, lunge, recover
groups.description: Stay at 45°, never vertical. Forearm on the back, not wrists. Beaten inside: around, never over.

groups.title: Passing under pressure
groups.description: Great passers freeze the defense until the last moment. Step away, step across, step back, step in — pick the one the splitter gives you.

groups.title: Shooting — release and deception
groups.description: Quick beats hard. Ball stays behind the head through the fake. Cross-face near-side every day; the draw shot and the dive progressions once the near-side is automatic.

groups.title: Dryland and conditioning
groups.description: Bands 15 minutes before every water session. Active stretching, never sit-and-hold. Dead Man Swimming when we want a fight.

groups.title: JV starter set
groups.description: The eight clips every JV player should know cold by October. Legs, one release, one defensive stance, one shot.

groups.title: ODP fundamentals — base position and movement
groups.description: USA Water Polo ODP's fundamentals: the base position for passing and shooting (Schroeder/Brooks), and the six movements every session should touch — eggbeater, short breaststroke kicks, spidering, skating, reverse sculling, ball handling.

practices.title: EXAMPLE — Monday after Walnut Hills
practices.intro: **This is a drafted example so you can see the shape; edit or delete it.** Watch the linked clips before practice — 6 minutes total. We are fixing two things from Sunday: hips dropping on perimeter defense, and slow releases when set has position.

blocks.title: Bands + active stretch
blocks.text: On deck before you get wet. Scarecrow rows, internal/external rotation, fake-throws. Nobody in the water without bands.

blocks.title: Legs: eggbeater, stepping, hip swings
blocks.text: Wide knees, still upper body. Stepping drill across the pool in a straight line at the surface. Hip swings — lead foot breaks the surface.

blocks.title: Perimeter defense: shoulder control → foul and deny
blocks.text: Pairs. Hand on the shoulder while he holds it, hands UP when he passes. Then add the foul-and-deny: hit the elbow, back over your hips at 45°, lane hand up. Referees will call the hold if your hips are down — that is the fix from Sunday.

blocks.title: Shooting: cross-face near-side
blocks.text: Shoulders to the cage before the ball arrives. Catch and release, no hesitation. Every rep.

blocks.title: 6-on-5 walk-through
blocks.text: Whiteboard first, then in the water at half speed. Whiteboard GIF goes here once we export one from WPA.

guides.title: Center offense - the Moody keys
guides.subtitle: Heather Moody's keys to the 2 m position, rewritten for St. X centers. Tap any timestamp to jump the player there.
guides.source: For St. X centers. Built 2026-09-10 by the Water Polo build chat from the transcript of "Water Polo: Center Offense Video USAWP Heather Moody" (24:22, YouTube `7QpmV2ELq4Y`, Peter Zamoyski's edit of Heather Moody's talk at the USA Water Polo winter meetings; Moody - Olympic gold 2012). The video's auto-captions are rough ("sinner" = center, "Lake strength" = leg strength); the wording below is a coach's rewrite, not a quote. Timestamps are for the clips worth actually watching.
guides.body:
**Five minutes to read. Then tap the four timestamps marked WATCH - the clips total under four minutes.**

---

## 1. What a good center is made of `0:32`
- **Legs.** You hold a defender up for the whole possession. No legs, no position.
- **Vision.** Know where the ball is the entire time and adjust before it moves, not after.
- **Patience.** Sometimes the ball cannot come in. Hold, wait, then attack the one window you get.
- **Play in the now.** Bad call, offensive foul, turnover - flush it and chase. A center who pouts for two seconds is a center who gives up a counter goal.
- **Controlled intensity.** Know when to be violent and when to be still.
- **Mental toughness.** A tight-called game, or a team that zones all night - you can play a whole game and never touch the ball. That is still your job.

## 2. Your two jobs `2:13`
1. **Gain ball side.** Your perimeter has to get the ball to the side you want to hold. Until then, you are setting up.
2. **Keep ball side.** Once the ball is there, holding it is on you. When the ball comes in: **explode to it.** That move gets the referee's attention (exclusion or foul), gets the separation, or gets the shot. A casual reach gets nothing.

## 3. Where you are `3:33`
Know your spot in front of the cage without looking. Shots go outside the post because the center did not know where he was. **Ideal: on the 3 m line, center cage.** You won't always get it, but that is what you are fighting for.

## 4. The chair - your base position `3:58` **WATCH**
Everything at center starts from here.
- **Sit in a chair.** Knees high, hips directly under you - not in front, not behind.
- **Hip bones to rib cage.** Squish them together. That curves your back the right way and rolls your shoulders forward.
- **Chin on your chest.** This is what stops the offensive foul - you never throw your head back, and when you snap, everything goes forward to the ball.
- **Shoulders out of the water.** Show the referee what the defender is doing to you.
- **Elbows high, level with your shoulders.** It makes you *wide*. A narrow center gets swum around. Wide, you cover your water and can dip and slide to cover more.
- **Hands sculling.**

Why the chair: you can hold this position all possession, and you snap and separate off it at a higher rate because you are over your legs.

## 5. Keep contact - you want his chest `2:52`
Ball-side position is established and kept by **keeping contact with the defender.** You want his chest on your back: you feel where he is about to move or jump and you counter it. If he has separation and only hands on your back, you can't read him.

## 6. The face-to-face start `6:57`
Most teams press. To save your legs, start **face to face**: arm to arm with the defender, **grip at his bicep/tricep**, and **keep space** between you.
- Not tight. Tight puts your hips on already, kills your snap into him, and turns it into a wrestling match.
- With space, when you go, you get momentum into him and he has to back off and reposition.
- **Use your off hand.** Most players turn slowly and lazily and the defender resets in a second. Inside arm goes to work aggressively, then the roadblock goes up (next section).
- You can sit here as long as the ball is on the far side. Conserve energy.

## 7. Turn, spin, seal `9:03` **WATCH**
The technique of the position. **Powerful and explosive** - you are driving into the defender to steal an inch of water and make him backpedal. Do it casually and he repositions or jumps back in front.
- **Turn.** Cage is behind you, ball is on one side. Your **inside arm** (the ball-side arm) goes to the **defender's outside armpit**. Pull him, put your shoulder into that armpit.
- **Spin.** Your shoulder is the navigator. **Put up the roadblock** - your body across his path so he cannot get back in front. Now the order is ball - you - defender. That water in front of you is yours.
- **Seal.** Back into the center spot, into your chair, ball side maintained.
- **Control him from armpit to hip.** Hand on that line; if he moves left, hook a little under the armpit and bring your chair with you, so if the ball comes you can still react.
- **The window is 3-5 seconds** from the ball reaching your side. Be explosive inside it. If it closes - zone, no entry - hold the chair and work on spreading the zone.
- **Anticipate the entry.** Know your passers. When you see it coming, snap to it and you get the separation.

## 8. Getting pushed out `5:38` **WATCH**
Hips down and vertical. If you go horizontal you lose - he pushes you off your spot. When he has your full back to push on, or you're losing contact:
- **Quarter turn.** Wide to narrow - now he only has a shoulder to push against.
- **Explosive breaststroke kick**, dive back in under his armpit, bring him with you.
- **Snap your shoulders square and re-set the chair.** You keep your water.
Don't turn and swim. Quarter turn, kick, dive back.

## 9. Fronted on the counter `12:38` **WATCH**
You come down the pool and the defender is waiting in front.
- **Get to 2 m, a little deep.** Let him take the front.
- **Move him out at 45°.** Never strength on strength straight back - you go nowhere. At 45° he often doesn't feel how far he's going, and now the ball can land where you have inside water. Ball comes to your side: inside arm, outside armpit, turn-spin-seal.
- **If the ball is already deep when you arrive, stop early** and go to work right there.
- **If he over-anticipates the pass** (jumps early): a quick **crossover**, dip back to the 45°, and he's beaten.
- **If he drifts too far from the goal or comes back inside to push:** **spin back toward the cage** to seal him off and keep ball side.
- **If he's quicker than your spin:** match his stroke, then take the hand closest to the ball and spin in. Always the roadblock.

## 10. Drawing the foul `17:08`
- **Hips stay underneath.** Defenders push your hips out of position. Answer with **one quick breaststroke kick** to drive them back - not a steady kick. Rhythm lets him time the jump around you.
- **Absorb the contact.** A lot of it happens underwater and gets no call. Keep your head up so you still know where the ball is.
- **Snap to the ball.** The thing even national teams struggle with. From the chair: drive your **left shoulder into his chest** (arms get a shoulder's length longer), **step with the right leg** (left if you're a lefty), scoop water. It makes the referee look, exposes what he's doing, and opens the shooting lane.
- **Take the chair with you.** Most centers snap without their base and there's nothing behind it. If he over-commits, you have no legs to finish the shot.

## 11. Shooting `18:59`
- **Where the defender is dictates the shot.** Behind you, fronting, on a side - each has its shot.
- **Where you are dictates the shot.** A quarter turn at 5 m is a hard finish. The same thing at 2 m is high percentage.
- **Know the pass.** Some come to your face, some are short, some you catch out of the air. Watch it in, control it - a bad pass doesn't have to be a turnover.

## 12. Against a zone `20:10`
You turn-spin-seal and they drop. Fine - the defense just honored you. Now your job is to **disrupt the zone**: **move across the cage**, not straight back to 2 m. Make the droppers follow you so your perimeter can see how far they really go. If someone crashes, you see it from your chair because you're on your legs - snap away from it and the ball is free.

## 13. Breaking the hold `21:09`
- **Quarter turn** exposes the suit grab to the referee; then dive back to position. If he still has it, spin back to face-to-face for a beat and go again.
- **Low hip grab:** spin away and drop the forearm - it breaks the hold, you separate, then get back.
- **In face-to-face and he's holding:** a quick **barrel roll toward his outside elbow.** He either lets go or it hurts. Don't sit there and hold back.
- **Don't jump and flail at the referee.** You lose your momentum and your position; the call may not come; and you've stopped working with your perimeter.

## 14. Look like the victim `23:04`
Big centers: sit a little lower in the water. Never look like the aggressor even when you are controlling everything.

## The card (memorize this)
1. **Chair:** knees high, hips under, chin down, shoulders out, elbows wide, hands sculling.
2. **His chest on your back.** Feel him.
3. **Face to face, arm to arm, with space.** Save your legs.
4. **Ball to your side = 3-5 seconds.** Inside arm to outside armpit. Turn, spin, roadblock, seal.
5. **Pushed out:** quarter turn, one kick, dive back, square up.
6. **Fronted:** 45°, never straight back.
7. **Snap to the ball with your chair.** Left shoulder in, right leg steps.
8. **Bad call? Flush it. Chase.**

*Watch order if you only watch four: 4 → 7 → 8 → 9.*
